unsavedChanges.description: This form holds changes that have not been saved yet. Leaving loses them.

nav.label: Admin navigation
nav.drawerDescription: The site’s admin sections, on a narrow screen.

reorder.failed: The order could not be saved.
reorder.stale: The list changed somewhere else. Reload and try again.

dashboard.unread: {count, plural, =0 {none unread} one {# unread} other {# unread}}
dashboard.featured: {count, plural, =0 {none featured} one {# featured} other {# featured}}
dashboard.profileMissing: No profile yet. Fill it in to create one.
dashboard.description: Everything the site holds, and what it still needs.
dashboard.linkCount: {count, plural, =0 {No social links} one {# social link} other {# social links}}
dashboard.readinessComplete: Everything the site needs is filled in.
dashboard.backgroundDescription: Written once, and worth a look when it changes.
dashboard.backgroundRow: {name}, {count, plural, =0 {nothing yet} one {# entry} other {# entries}}

profile.title: Profile

fields.headline: Headline
fields.emailPublic: Show the email on the site
fields.locationPublic: Show the location on the site
fields.availabilityPublic: Show the availability on the site

profile.description: The details the public site shows about you.
profile.altHint: Describe the photograph for anyone who cannot see it. Leave blank if it is purely decorative.
profile.emptyDescription: Your name, headline and photo are what the site opens with. Fill them in to create the profile.

resume.title: Resume
resume.hint: A PDF, up to 5 MB. It is offered as a download rather than opened in the browser.

contact.hint: Each detail is stored either way. The box beside it decides whether the public site is allowed to show it — the contact form works whether or not your address is on the page.
contact.emailPublicHint: An address on a public page is collected by scrapers within days. Left off, the contact form is still how people reach you.
contact.locationPublicHint: A city is usually fine; a street address is not something a portfolio needs.
contact.availabilityPublicHint: A status exists to be seen. Turn it off to keep it to yourself for now.
contact.title: Contact

projects.title: Projects
projects.description: What you have built, and the skills each one used.
projects.altHint: Describe each image for anyone who cannot see it. Leave blank if the image is purely decorative.
projects.slugHint: The readable half of the project’s URL: /projects/your-address. Suggested from the title while you write it, and yours to change. Change it after the project is published and anyone who saved the old link loses it.
projects.storyHint: What you did, what made it hard, what you decided and what changed. Leave any of them blank — an empty field says less than a filled one that says nothing. The approach is worth the most: name the decision and the obvious alternative you rejected.

gallery.title: Gallery
gallery.empty: No screenshots yet. Add the first one.
gallery.full: That is the maximum. Remove one to add another.

projects.confirmDescription: The project and its images are removed from the site. This cannot be undone.
projects.emptyDescription: Projects are the work the site shows, each with a cover, a gallery and the skills it used.

stack.title: Built with
stack.empty: No technologies or tools exist yet. Add some on those pages first.

socialLinks.title: Social links
socialLinks.description: Where else you can be found.
socialLinks.confirmDescription: The link is removed from the site. This cannot be undone.
socialLinks.emptyDescription: Links are where else the site points people — a profile, a repository, a site of your own.

messages.title: Messages
messages.unreadCount: {count, plural, =0 {All read} one {# unread} other {# unread}}
messages.description: What people sent through the contact form.
messages.emptyDescription: Anything sent through the contact form arrives here.
messages.selectPrompt: Choose a message to read it
messages.confirmDescription: The message is removed for good. This cannot be undone.

login.title: Admin sign in
login.subtitle: Enter your credentials to manage the portfolio.

expertise.confirmDescription: It is removed from the site. This cannot be undone.
expertise.inUse: {count, plural, one {# project still uses} other {# projects still use}} this. Unlink it there first.

skill.title: Skills
skill.description: What you can do — capabilities and methodologies, not the tools you do them with.
skill.emptyDescription: Skills are capabilities and methodologies — System Architecture, Problem Solving. The languages and frameworks belong under Technologies.

technology.title: Technologies
technology.description: The languages, frameworks and stores your work is built out of.
technology.emptyDescription: Technologies are what a project is built out of — TypeScript, React, PostgreSQL. Each carries its own brand logo.

tool.title: Tools
tool.description: The software you operate, rather than build with.
tool.emptyDescription: Tools are the software you operate — Git, Docker, Figma. Each carries its own brand logo.

experience.title: Experience
experience.description: Where you have worked, most recent first. The dates are the order.
experience.emptyDescription: Each position is a role at an organisation, with the months you held it. They are listed most recent first, so there is nothing to order by hand.
experience.confirmDescription: The position and its dates ({period}) are removed from the site. This cannot be undone.
experience.currentHint: Tick this if you still hold the position. It has no end date while you do.
experience.endHint: Cleared while the position is current.

education.title: Education
education.description: Where you studied, most recent first. The dates are the order.
education.emptyDescription: Each entry is a qualification from an institution, with the months you studied for it. They are listed most recent first, so there is nothing to order by hand.
education.confirmDescription: The entry and its dates ({period}) are removed from the site. This cannot be undone.
education.currentHint: Tick this if you are still studying. It has no end date while you are.
education.endHint: Cleared while the course is in progress.

credentials.confirmDescription: It is removed from the site. This cannot be undone.
credentials.expiryHint: Leave blank if it does not expire. An expiry in the past is fine — it is marked as expired rather than refused.

certification.title: Certifications
certification.description: What you have been certified in, most recently issued first.
certification.emptyDescription: A certification is awarded by a body that can verify it — AWS, Microsoft, the Linux Foundation. Each carries the date it was issued and, if it has one, the date it expires.

course.title: Courses
course.description: What you have completed, most recently issued first.
course.emptyDescription: A course is something you finished rather than something you were certified in — a platform, a workshop, a training programme. Courses rarely expire; leave the expiry blank.

languages.title: Languages
languages.description: What you speak, in the order you want them read.
languages.emptyDescription: Each entry is a language and how well you speak it, on the CEFR scale. The order is yours to choose — there are no dates to sort by.
languages.confirmDescription: It is removed from the site. This cannot be undone.

options.title: Option lists
options.description: The choices behind every dropdown in the admin. What you add here becomes selectable everywhere it belongs.
options.emptyDescription: An option is a code the content stores and a label the reader sees. Add the first one to make it choosable.
options.confirmDescription: It disappears from the dropdown that offers it. Anything already using it keeps it, and removal is refused while anything does.
options.inUse: {rows, plural, one {One entry still uses this option} other {# entries still use this option}}, so it cannot be removed.
options.codeHint: Lowercase letters, digits and dashes. This is what the content stores, and it cannot be changed afterwards.
options.codeFixed: Fixed at creation — the content already stored points at it.

account.title: Account
account.description: The account you sign in with, and the devices it is signed in on.
account.signedInDescription: This address is also your login. Changing it signs out every other device.
account.emailHint: There is no confirmation email, so check it carefully — a wrong address is the one you will have to sign in with.
account.emailChanged: Address changed. Sign in with the new one from now on.
account.passwordDescription: Changing it signs out every other device. This one stays signed in.
account.passwordHint: At least {count} characters. A long phrase beats a short puzzle.
account.passwordChanged: Password changed. Every other device has been signed out.
account.sessionsDescription: Signs out every browser and device except this one. Use it if you have left yourself signed in somewhere you no longer control.
account.sessionsRevoked: Every other device has been signed out.
account.mailDescription: How the site reaches you when someone uses the contact form.
account.mailOffHint: Messages are still stored and shown in the inbox — nothing is lost. To be emailed as well, fill in the mail block in .env and restart the backend.
account.mailHint: Settings live in .env rather than here: a password kept in the database can be read back out of it, and out of every backup. Sending a test is the only way to know the credentials still work — they are only ever wrong at the moment they are used.
account.mailSent: Sent to {address}. If it does not arrive, check the spam folder before changing anything.
account.mailNotConfigured: No mail server is configured, so there was nothing to send with.
account.mailSendFailed: The mail server refused the message. The credentials or the host may be wrong, or the server may be down.
